change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme colour of embedded-post topic meta links changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: The diff changes the first argument of the `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` colour from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (removed line) to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The light theme therefore renders these bold links light grey instead of dark. The PR body says only that the dark-theme branch must use $secondary, so the light value should not change. The other 27-odd hunks keep the light value. Restore the light argument to 30%. The dark branch is also out of pattern: the 30% light value is paired with secondary 70% everywhere else (app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/user.scss:119, app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:15), so `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` is the consistent form.
findings.originReason: The base used 30% light. This diff rewrote the line with a 70% light value.

verification.reason: Base line 291 was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Head line 291 changes the light branch to 70%, with secondary 30% for dark, so the light theme's bold meta links go from dark to light grey. Elsewhere a 30% light value is paired with secondary 70% (common/base/user.scss:119, common/base/topic-post.scss:15).

findings.title: Mobile .custom-message-length light-theme value inverted from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The removed line was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, so the light theme's character-count hint becomes near full-strength text. The desktop counterpart (app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss:94) keeps 70% light and 30% dark. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to match desktop. The mobile dark branch (secondary 70%) is the inverse of desktop's, so it should follow desktop too.
findings.originReason: The base light value was 70%. This diff changed it to 30%.

verification.reason: Base mobile/modal.scss:102 used primary 70%. Head line 102 uses primary 30% for light and secondary 70% for dark, which inverts the old light value. Desktop modal.scss:94 in head keeps 70%/30%.

findings.title: Mobile .topic-map h3 light-theme colour changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The removed line was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new light branch is 50%, so the light-theme topic-map section headings are noticeably lighter. The PR body does not describe this. The desktop heading for the same selector (app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:321) uses 20% light and 80% secondary, so the dark branch here (secondary 50%) also differs from the pattern used for a 20% colour. Restore to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to match desktop.
findings.originReason: The base light value was 20%. This diff changed it to 50%.

verification.reason: Base mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (.topic-map h3) was primary 20%. Head uses 50%/50%, so the light-theme headings get lighter. The desktop counterpart at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 uses 20%/80%.

findings.title: Mobile .group-member-info .name light-theme colour changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The removed line was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch is 50%, so group member names become lighter in the light theme. The PR body only describes the dark-theme branch. The dark branch here (secondary 50%) is also not the mirror of 30%, which is 70% (see app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/user.scss:119). Restore the light value to 30%, and use `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark branch. The same change appears in desktop (see the desktop/user.scss finding).
findings.originReason: The base light value was 30%. This diff changed it to 50%.

verification.reason: Base mobile/user.scss:497 (.group-member-info .name) was primary 30%. Head line 497 uses 50%/50%, which lightens names in the light theme and breaks the 30%/70% pairing used elsewhere (common/base/user.scss:119).

findings.title: Desktop .group-member-info .name light-theme colour changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The removed line was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light branch is 50%, so names in the group member list on desktop become lighter in the light theme. The PR body only describes the dark branch. The dark branch (secondary 50%) is not the mirror of 30% (70%, as used at app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/user.scss:119). Restore the light value to 30%, and use `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark branch. The same change is in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497.
findings.originReason: The base light value was 30%. This diff changed it to 50%.

verification.reason: Base desktop/user.scss:522 (.group-member-info .name) was primary 30%. Head line 522 uses 50%/50%, so the light-theme value changes and the dark branch is not the 70% mirror.

contracts.action: dark-light-choose(light, dark) replaces single scale-color($primary, ...) colour declarations across the stylesheets in this part
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/variables.scss:46-52 (the function) and the pre-existing use of the same pattern at app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:84
contracts.before_after: Before: the declaration always used the primary-derived colour. After: dark-light-choose returns the first argument when brightness($primary) < brightness($secondary) and the second argument otherwise, so dark themes get a secondary-derived colour. In the light theme the output should be unchanged, except for the five lines flagged in this review.
contracts.visible_effect: Colours of text, borders and icons change only in dark themes, across roughly 30 stylesheets.
contracts.failure_mode: Dark-theme colours are now computed from $secondary using mirrored percentages (N% primary paired with (100-N)% secondary). Contrast in dark themes has not been checked, because rendering is out of scope for a read-only review.
contracts.open_question: Do the mirrored secondary-based values give acceptable text contrast in dark themes? This needs a rendered check that a read-only review cannot do.

summary:
I read all 32 stylesheets in full. The change makes the dark-theme branch of colour declarations use $secondary through dark-light-choose, which matches the PR body. Most hunks keep the light-theme value unchanged. Five hunks also change the light-theme value, which the PR body does not describe, and each one is a visible regression in the light theme:
- desktop/topic-post.scss:291 (30% → 70%)
- mobile/modal.scss:102 (70% → 30%)
- mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20% → 50%)
- mobile/user.scss:497 (30% → 50%)
- desktop/user.scss:522 (30% → 50%)

Each is reported as a "fix". Nothing was built or run. Dark-theme contrast is unverified and is recorded as an open contract. No ADRs exist in the repository (no docs/adr directory).
